title: ai-badger project config
description: Project profile authored by the agent during welcome-ai-badger and validated by scripts. The single machine-readable input the scaffolded skills read.

frameworkVersion.description: ai-badger framework version this config was generated against.

domain.description: One-line business/domain description; NOT a stack.

commonStacks.description: Catalog stack(s) always resolved in addition to `stacks` — the source of the always-included stack's name for scaffold.py and install_plugins.py. Defaults to "common" when absent.

stacks.description: Selected technology stacks. Must exist under index.json.stacks (excluding 'common').

agents.description: Coding agents detected as present in the repo/user scope; only these are initialized. Keep in sync with AGENT_NAMES in badger_lib.py.

projectUrl.description: Board/project URL; gates project-board task features.

skillScope.description: default = honor each skill entry's declared scope; local = force all installs to project scope. Renamed from pluginScope in v0.7.0.

include.description: Catalog items this project asks for by index name — the counterpart of exclude. Skills declaring scope: optIn in their own SKILL.md frontmatter can be named — they stay in the catalog until a project wants them (ADR-0018) — as can a group name from badger_lib.SKILL_GROUPS, which delivers every member. Both welcome-ai-badger and den-refresh deliver what is named here, and a name matching no optIn skill — or naming one that already ships by default — is reported, never fatal. exclude wins if a name appears in both.

skills.description: optIn skill names to scaffold into .ai-badger/skills/. A name in badger_lib.SKILL_GROUPS installs its whole group — those skills read each other's references/ in place and cannot work alone — and a group's own name (e.g. "documentation") works too.

exclude.description: Catalog items this project declines, by index name. Neither welcome-ai-badger nor den-refresh delivers them again, and the discovery links ai-badger placed for them are removed; the copy already under .ai-badger/ is left on disk. Only the four name-addressable feature types can be declined — templates, hooks and adjustments materialise outputs named otherwise. A name matching nothing in the catalog is reported, never fatal.

skills.description: Skill names not to scaffold into .ai-badger/skills/.

personas.description: Persona names not to scaffold into .ai-badger/agents/.

invariants.description: Invariant names not to scaffold into .ai-badger/invariants/ or render into the agent instruction files.

instructions.description: Instruction names not to scaffold into .ai-badger/instructions/.

mcp.description: What this project wants done about the MCP servers the catalog declares (ADR-0014). Not the same concern as mcpToolIndex, which curates whatever servers arrive; this decides which of them the agent may call. Each host honours it as far as its own surface allows: Claude denies project-wide in .claude/settings.json, Copilot leaves the server out of .github/mcp.json, and Hermes gets a proposed tools exclude because it has no project route at all.

approve.description: Pre-approve the servers ai-badger declares into this project's .mcp.json, so their tools do not prompt: Claude Code's enabledMcpjsonServers plus a permissions.allow rule per server. Set false to keep the prompt for a project that declares a server but wants each call confirmed.

decline.description: Server names whose tools this project refuses, by name, whatever route the server arrived by — catalog declaration, plugin, user-global config or CLI. A declined server is not declared at all, and comes back out of .mcp.json and .github/mcp.json if an earlier run wrote it; on Claude it also lands as disabledMcpjsonServers plus a permissions.deny rule, and deny beats allow. This is the decline route config.externalTools' silence used to carry (issue #186).

mcpToolIndex.description: MCP tool index configuration. When enabled, the mcp-index skill and ai_badger_hooks plugin use index-based tool recommendations.

path.description: Relative path to the index file within the project.

agentDocs.description: Size budget for the generated agent discovery files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, HERMES.md, .hermes.md, copilot-instructions.md), enforced by the task skill's stop hook. Omit for the defaults. Raise it when the breach comes from framework-rendered content the project cannot shorten without declining policy: these files are regenerated in full, so editing them does not reduce their size past the next re-scaffold. A non-positive or non-integer value is ignored and the default applies, so a typo cannot silently disable the gate.

maxChars.description: Character budget per agent discovery file.

maxLines.description: Line budget per agent discovery file.

statusLineCapture.description: Capture Claude Code's statusLine payload so the task skill can read its rate-limit metadata instead of spending a probe. When enabled, scaffolding points .claude/settings.json statusLine at ai-badger's capture wrapper and records the renderer it replaced as the wrapper's delegate, so the existing status line keeps rendering.

enabled.description: Wire the capture wrapper into .claude/settings.json. Off by default: statusLine is a personal setting and a project-level entry overrides the user's own.
